candidates.title: Organize workflow template rejection feedback

demandEvidence.chore: Organize feedback after repeated workflow-template submission rejections into a revision checklist.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’m looking for some guidance regarding a workflow template submission that has been rejected three times.

ease.reason: A student could test a simple checklist with manually supplied rejection notes; the post gives no criteria or tool support.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: workflow authors may pay for submission guidance, but one request shows neither wider demand nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock could organize supplied rejection notes, though the actual criteria and template are absent.

autonomy.reason: A checklist could flag entered items, but a person must interpret rejection reasons; no automation capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The post directly reports three template rejections and asks for guidance, but provides no rejection reasons or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a checklist can organize author-supplied rejection notes, but the post omits the criteria and template needed for useful guidance; no supplied building reference supports automation.

candidates.title: Summarize failed subscription invoices

demandEvidence.chore: Summarize attempted but failed subscription invoices over a 90-day period to estimate declined-card revenue.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I made a tool to show how much revenue declined cards are costing your SaaS. You make a read-only Stripe key, and it totals every subscription invoice from the last 90 days that was attempted, failed,

ease.reason: A beginner could prototype a failed-invoice summary from synthetic rows, but real Stripe access and metric definitions are not documented.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: SaaS operators may pay for recovered-revenue analysis; the post shows a maker-built tool, not willingness to pay for a service.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock could total supplied failed invoices, while Stripe integration and accurate revenue attribution remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A repeated invoice summary is conceivable, but no supported integration is supplied and a person must verify records and conclusions.

evidence.reason: The excerpt describes a read-only Stripe key and attempted, failed invoices, but its text is truncated and gives no validated demand.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the excerpt describes a maker’s tool and a bounded invoice summary, but does not establish unmet professional-services demand, validated use, or implementation support.

candidates.title: Compare team software costs and replacements

demandEvidence.chore: Compare what teams pay for software with what replaced it.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: what teams pay for software and what replaced it

ease.reason: A beginner could test a report with manually entered software and replacement rows, but the post gives no data fields or implementation method.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional-services teams may pay to understand software spend and replacements; this single Show HN title proves no service demand or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype could compare operator-supplied synthetic inventory rows; importing real contracts or validating savings is outside the evidence.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable comparison and summary could be automated on supplied rows, but data entry and checking whether replacements are equivalent need a person.

evidence.reason: The captured title gives a bounded software-spend and replacement comparison task, but no inputs, frequency, constraints, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed a proposed report from operator-supplied software and replacement rows; the title supports a bounded comparison task but gives no workflow details or implementation evidence, so the provisional scores remain below threshold.
